sentences.text: Cristian Barrientos Pozo, a Chilean executive, was named President and Chief Executive Officer of Wal-Mart de Mexico, S.A.B. de C.V.
(BMV/BIVA: WALMEX) on October 7, 2025, after serving as interim leader and board member since August 1, 2025.

He joined Walmart Chile in 1999, led the creation of the Super Bodega aCuenta format in 2007, and moved to Walmart Mexico in 2012 as vice president of Bodega Aurrera operations, becoming senior vice president in 2016 across the three Bodega formats.

sentences.quote: In 2018, Barrientos became General Manager of Walmart Central America, leading operations across five countries during a challenging period. He returned to Mexico in 2020 as Director of Operations.
sentences.text: He was promoted to general manager of Walmart Central America in 2018 and returned to Mexico as chief operating officer in 2020, and from early 2023 he served as CEO of Walmart Chile.

sentences.text: Cristian Barrientos Pozo, a 26-year Walmart veteran who ran Bodega Aurrera operations, Central America and Chile, became Walmex CEO in October 2025 after Ignacio Caride's unexpected resignation, having served as interim chief executive since 1 August, continuing as a provisional board member pending ratification at the annual shareholders' meeting.
Execution has been uneven: 2025 capex of 39 billion pesos trailed the 41.8 billion planned because of delayed store and technology projects, a year the company itself described as "not so good."
For 2026 it guided to about 43 billion pesos, weighted to remodels (42%), new units (26%), supply-chain automation (24%) and technology (8%), plus a proposed buyback of up to 10 billion pesos.
